title: Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur
short_description: Chola-period Shaiva temple, vimana rising 66 m. Granite quarried inland, transported via the Kaveri delta during the northeast monsoon.

title: Borobudur Stupa
short_description: Mahayana stupa-mandala, Sailendra dynasty, Central Java. Reliefs depict monsoon-trade ships of the Indian Ocean network.

title: Hokusai, 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa'
short_description: Polychrome woodblock print. Edo-period engagement with imported Prussian blue pigment along late-monsoon-era trade routes.

title: Patola silk, Patan
short_description: Double-ikat silk produced in Gujarat, traded along the monsoon route to Maluku in exchange for cloves and nutmeg.

title: The Spice Route from Malabar to Aden
short_description: Indian Ocean shipping lane that depended on the southwest monsoon for outbound voyages and the northeast monsoon for return.

title: Rajendra Chola I
short_description: Chola emperor whose naval expeditions to Srivijaya (1025) exploited monsoon timing; patron of Brihadisvara and Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
short_description: Greek navigational text describing Indian Ocean monsoon trade routes and port cities. The earliest surviving practical sailing guide for the region.

title: Angkor Wat
short_description: Khmer temple complex aligned to the equinox sunrise. Reservoir system (barays) calibrated to monsoon flood cycles.
